title: Rav Chinena bar Shelamya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a distinguished student of Rav who always spoke in Rav’s name, as in Shabbat 43b and 123a, Pesachim 105a, Beitzah 31b and 32b, Bava Batra 111a, Chullin 37b (there Rav Chanina), Niddah 65a, Bekhorot 24b (there Rav Chananya), Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 1:6 (there Chananyah), Beitzah 1:5 and Sanhedrin, chapter 1, end of halakhah 2. In Sanhedrin 77a, “Rav Chinena bar Yehudah said in Rav’s name,” and Dikdukei Soferim cites from a manuscript Rav Chinena bar Shelamyah. In Eruvin 98b: “Rav Chinena bar Shelamya taught Chiyya bar Rav before Rav,” and Rav said to him, “You have abandoned the Rabbis and acted like Rabbi Meir?” In the Jerusalem Talmud there, 1:1, folio 5a: “Chananyah bar Shilmiya was sitting teaching Chiyya the son of Rav; Rav put his head out of the window and said to him: It is not so. He said to him: And shall we not teach it so (in our Mishnah)? He said to him: Teach it (if you learn, you will know it is not so).” In Niddah 25a he said to Rav: “According to whom does the Master hold?” etc.

Hyman counts him among Rav’s choicest students, as in Pesachim 105a, where they said: Rav Chananya bar Shelamya and Rav’s students were sitting at a meal, and Rav Hamnuna the Elder was standing over them. They said to him: “Go see whether the day has been sanctified.” He said to them: “You need not.” Rav Amram said to them: “Thus said Rav.”

Hyman suggests that apparently he remained in Sura after Rav’s death and did not go to study before Shmuel, but only sent his questions from there to Shmuel, as in Sanhedrin 24b: “Rav Chinena bar Shelamyah said: They sent from the school of Rav to Shmuel: Let our master teach us.” Hyman finds no conversation with Rav Huna and takes this as a sign that he died before Rav Huna headed the academy in Sura.

notes.text: שלחו ליה רב is rendered from the school of Rav, as disclosed in the original note. Always in Rav’s name has Chinena as transmitter, not Rav as his own source. All title/name variants and Hyman’s chronological inference from non-mention of Huna are attributed rather than a fresh corpus absence claim.

The consulted Pesachim 105a meal account continues with Rav’s rule and Rav Amram’s distinction between kiddush and havdalah. Hyman’s abridgment is retained. Always speaking in Rav’s name has Chinena as transmitter. The school-of-Rav reading stays disclosed, while non-mention of Huna and the resulting academy chronology remain Hyman’s bounded argument, not a fresh exhaustive absence finding.
